transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The Attorney General of New York is now leading a criminal investigation into an alleged gang
rape at a Cornell University fraternity house.
As NPR's Brian Mann explains, New York Governor Kathy Hochul says she appointed A.G. Letitia
James in the hopes of finding out why the 2024 case was not fully investigated.
Hochul says she's troubled by the behavior of university leaders, campus police and a
local prosecutor who dropped the investigation two years ago after seeing only a partial
transcript of the woman's allegations.
I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug.
Letitia James, the state attorney general, will now take over the criminal probe.
Hochul says she'll also push to close a loophole in state law that makes it harder to prosecute
sex crimes when the victim has been drinking or using drugs.
Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape, period.
Cornell University has also agreed to Hochul's demand that an outside counsel review the
school's handling of the case.
Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
The U.S. bond market is showing some relief after the government's latest jobs report
eased concerns about a potentially overheating economy that pushes inflation higher.
NPR's Scott Horsley has more.
The U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs last month.
That's weaker than forecasters were expecting.
And job gains for both July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000.
The updated figures now show a net loss of jobs during the month of July.
We're still not seeing a massive number of layoffs across the economy, but most industries
just aren't doing a lot of hiring either.
That's NPR's Scott Horsley reporting.
Looking at Wall Street, we see the Dow is up 188 points, S&P has risen 59, the Nasdaq
is up 347 points, or 1.2 percent.
Democrats are expanding the map of congressional races that they say could be winnable in this
fall's midterm elections.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports the new list includes 66 districts.
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is pushing into traditionally Republican territory,
adding districts in Kansas, North Carolina, Texas and Oklahoma, among others, to its districts
in play list.
That is a list of congressional districts where the party committee thinks it can be
competitive.
It doesn't mean the Democratic candidates in these races have an easy path to victory,
but it does mean Democrats are bullish about their chances overall.
Republicans are projecting confidence as well, with Speaker Mike Johnson traveling around
the country, saying he thinks his party will expand its House majority.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
Yesterday, President Trump was in Texas and Oklahoma, and Vice President J.D. Vance was
in Florida.
It's NPR News.
G7 leaders say they plan to release 100 million barrels of oil beginning with substantial amounts
of diesel.
The fuel's record high prices in the wake of wars in the Middle East and Eastern Europe
have hit global delivery networks hard, including in the United States where many farmers say
they are struggling to afford diesel.
Amazon's pledging a billion-dollar investment in data center communities as the facility's
heavy reliance on electricity and water face public pushback this midterm election year.
Executive Matt Garman says in a blog post today that Amazon is no longer using non-disclosure
agreements with government partners on projects.
Studies in the Democratic Republic of Congo say that more than 4,000 people have died
from Ebola in the Central African nation.
Michael Koloki has the latest.
The latest Ebola death toll figures come in the wake of several strikes by health workers
in the country.
Earlier this week, the workers held a protest in the Ituri Province, the epicenter of the
outbreak, over what they called delayed wage payments.
Meanwhile the United Nations has accused members of the country's military of recently burning
down a transit center for Ebola patients in the east of the country, as soldiers carried
out a search for weapons in the area.
And the World Health Organization has raised concern about the Ebola virus spreading rapidly
into new health zones in Congo, stretching already limited resources.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Koloki in Nairobi.

U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs last month, easing concerns about economic overheating and inflation
Democrats expand list of winnable congressional districts to 66 seats in traditionally Republican territory
G7 leaders plan to release 100 million barrels of oil to address record high diesel prices
Amazon pledges billion-dollar investment in data center communities and ends non-disclosure agreements with government
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak
